observedArticle.headline: Meta launches personal AI agent, Muse, emphasizes safety and privacy
findings: AP independently reported the United States launch and described Muse as available through its own app or WhatsApp.
AP explained the industry distinction between a chatbot that answers and an agent that can take actions using a language model and software tools.
AP framed adoption as unresolved; the article did not independently test Meta's security design or establish that approval prompts always prevent mistakes.
AP reported an 18-and-over audience, but no current Meta terms or help page was recovered to support that restriction as a primary product rule. The candidate therefore omits the age claim.
exactExcerpts: Meta launched on Tuesday a personal artificial intelligence agent, Muse
which for now is only available in the U.S.
People can message the agent in a separate app, called Muse, or message it in WhatsApp.
Tech companies are touting AI agents as the next step after chatbots
The question is, will people actually use it?

limitation: This browser observation records AP's complete article text and line locators. It is independent reporting, not a product test, and direct archival capture was blocked by the publisher.
